kandidaty.zagolovok: [AINews] Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
kandidaty.tekst:
AINews by Latent Space

Scott Aaronson was still trying to digest two proofs of VP ≠ VNP at dinner. Before dessert, an OpenAI paper claimed that the square matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4. During dessert, another paper claimed matching upper and lower bounds for the finite Fourier transform. The lower bound is the biggest news. In October, OpenAI found an upper bound for ω down to at most 9/4. Finding the lower bound = upper bound leaves only one possible value, which is a shocking result for most.

We plotted 64 selected AI-assisted research advances so far this year. November accounts for 20, including six preprints from Google’s Cogentic. The curve follows public releases, including proofs still under review. We count the two VP ≠ VNP proofs once and give October’s faster matrix multiplication algorithm and November’s matching lower bound an entry each.

The big releases underline how much a paper count can hide. OpenAI’s catalogue lists 730 manuscripts across 375 result families, including follow-ups and companion arguments. Its revision log also records three October withdrawals after a sign error in one paper affected two others. Yupan Liu showed that two messages suffice for quantum interactive proofs, a result that would have been a big deal on its own. Aaronson says Liu used AI and that he had to remind himself the result had even happened.

In other big news, today’s guest Thariq Shihipar announced his big move from Anthropic to OpenAI, the second high profile Ant→OAI move in recent times after Cat Wu. We dive into his two philosophies of AI and how and where /humans add taste.

AI News for 11/25/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space. You can opt in/out of email frequencies!

AI Twitter Recap

AI-Generated Math Results: Matmul Exponent, Factoring and Lean Proofs

Matrix multiplication exponent: OpenAI's model claims a lower bound matching its October upper bound, making ω exactly 9/4. Previously no nontrivial lower bound was known (@SebastienBubeck; repo).

Mechanism: The result reportedly comes through an explicit superlinear circuit lower bound (@wjmzbmr1).

Implications: Bubeck notes that a prior Lee et al. result implies LPs solvable in n^{9/4}. He also says LPs can now be solved in strongly polynomial time, a Smale problem (follow-up).

Expert reaction: Omri Weinstein calls it "truly surreal" if correct, since most experts expected ω = 2 (@WeinsteinOmri).

OpenAI batch: Nine new papers with Lean proofs came out a day after a claimed VP ≠ VNP proof (summary).

Other claims: Fourier transform complexity of n√log n (@lreyzin).

Integer multiplication: Also n√log n, tight under weak ETH (@cloneofsimo).

Same-day solutions: Anthropic posted its own VP ≠ VNP solution the same day (@vitaliychiley).

Frontier Models as Research Engines: VP ≠ VNP, Protein Design and 948 Kernel Bugs

VP ≠ VNP, posted by two labs: An Anthropic GitHub repo reportedly contains a proof by an internal Claude research model that VP ≠ VNP. This is the algebraic analogue of P vs NP, posed by Valiant in 1979, and implies that polynomials such as the permanent lack small circuits over every field (@kimmonismus, repo pointer).

OpenAI's counter-release: OpenAI then posted its own proof and says it was "obtained on November 6, 2026." Neither lab named a model or published an announcement (@AndrewCurran_).

Scope: The result does not imply P ≠ NP, which still requires general Boolean circuit lower bounds (@ZhihuFrontier).

Speculation: Curran argues that both labs are sitting on unreleased results and repeats unconfirmed rumors of cryptography breakthroughs. Treat this as opinion.

Riemann proof clarifications: Levent Alpöge says the "250,000+ pages" claim was a joke. He released only the Lean code because he could not produce a readable writeup, and called it "full of garbage obviously, but compiles" (@kimmonismus, @simonw).

Lineage claim: A Zhihu analysis traces Alpöge's key method to a short OpenAI proof excluding Landau–Siegel zeros. This is an attributed inference (@ZhihuFrontier).

GPT-6 protein design, wet-lab validated: OpenAI released a preprint showing GPT-6 models designing new protein shapes and sequences through reasoning and code, without specialized bio models (@OpenAI).

Results: 14 of 107 resequenced proteins showed binding. 128 of 182 redesigned small antibodies and 179 of 272 antibody fragments retained binding (details).

Cost caveat: On a prior DNA task, GPT-6.1 Sol was about 2,000x more expensive per task than a specialized model (@_lewtun).

It’s now obvious that we’ll be getting, not one-off solutions to this or that complexity question, but a whole new continent of mathematical truth, one that we’d previously only glimpsed through fog. Picture van Leeuwenhoek first training a microscope on pondwater, or Galileo first training his telescope on the stars. That might give you some idea of how our resolution into the complexity-theoretic universe, and the whole universe of mathematical truth beyond it, has now improved.

kandidaty.tekst:
@testingcatalog: AI Agents powered by Living Brain have proved 17 math results, including the Lindelöf hypothesis, Erdős Problem 985, and Euler’s idoneal numbers.

Living Brain is a memory tool for AI agents, developed by ChatAndBuild.

The team spent months adding math papers and open problems to @livingbrain. When the proof came out, Living Brain pointed out to the agents which problems were now within reach.

This happened within three days of the new Riemann Hypothesis proof. Six of the problems were long-standing, with some open for over 100 years.

Цитирует @ladyxtel: Three days after the Riemann Hypothesis was proved in Lean, our agents had used it to prove 17 results.

Six are named conjectures that were open until 20 November, including the Lindelöf hypothesis, Erdős Problem 985 and Euler’s idoneal numbers.

Some had been open for more than 100 years.

@livingbrain held the memory, OpenHuman’s agents wrote the proofs, and Lean checked every one.
